belief: I'm less of a man (or woman) because of this.
origins: Disability can challenge roles as provider, protector, caregiver, or athlete. Society’s images of strength can make us feel less masculine or feminine, especially when injury or illness changes how we work, parent, or relate.
teaches: “God created man in His own image… male and female He created them.” Your identity as a man or woman in God’s image does not depend on strength or ability. “The parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable, and the parts we consider less honorable, we treat with greater honor.” “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” “When I am weak, then I am strong.” Courage, love, faithfulness, and character are the real marks of maturity.
self_statements: I cannot be what I should be.
A real man (or woman) would not need this.
errors: Believing I am either fully a man or woman or less.
Predicting that others will see me as less.
Feeling diminished and concluding that I am.
questions: What does manhood or womanhood mean to me, and where did I learn it?
What qualities of character do I still show?
How do my loved ones see me?
What roles can I fulfill differently?
What does Scripture say about identity and weakness?
What new role might God give me?
truth: My identity as a man or woman is a gift from God, not a measure of strength. I can serve my family and others in new ways, with courage and character.
hw_truths: I am made in God’s image.
log: Each week, note one way you served or loved.
actions: Write what you have lost and what remains.
prayer: Father, I feel diminished. Remind me that I am Your image-bearer, and show me how to love and serve in my new circumstances. Amen.
